title.en: Moving averages and the trend of a time series

heading.en: Ice cream sales through the year

hook.en: An ice-cream seller's sales rise every summer and fall every monsoon. Is the business growing? Smoothing the quarter-to-quarter ups and downs shows the *trend*.

objectives.en: Choose the period to match the cycle

say.en: An ice-cream seller's sales rise every summer and fall every monsoon. Is the business growing? Smoothing the quarter-to-quarter ups and downs shows the trend. In this lesson: Compute odd-period moving averages.
Compute centred even-period moving averages.
Choose the period to match the cycle.

body.en: A time series often has a long-term trend plus regular (seasonal or cyclical) fluctuations. A k-period *moving* average replaces each value by the mean of k consecutive values, sliding one step at a time. For odd k the average is placed against the middle period. For even k (e.g. 4 quarters) the averages fall between periods, so they are centred by averaging successive pairs. Choosing k equal to the length of the cycle removes the regular fluctuation and shows the trend; values at the ends are lost.

points.en: Odd k: placed at the middle period
Even k: centre by averaging pairs

prompt.en: Put the steps of a centred 4-quarter moving average in order.

steps.en: Write the quarterly data in time order.
Add four consecutive values at a time, sliding by one.
Divide each 4-quarter total by 4 (these fall between quarters).
Average each successive pair of these to centre them.
Place the centred averages against quarters 3, 4, … and plot the trend.
